title: Luk chup
summary: Luk chup are tiny fruits and vegetables modelled from sweetened mung-bean paste, painted with food colour and dipped in clear agar jelly so they shine. Paint each pale fruit its own colour, add stalks, leaves and highlights, then watch the glaze go on.
howToPlay: Look at the framed picture: it shows the finished tray of fruits.
Tap a colour to dip the brush, then press and drag to paint. Slow, steady strokes lay a fat line; the line thins as the paint runs out, so dip again.
Fill each pale fruit with its colour: brush inside it or tap the fruit to flood it.
Press Next, then add green stalks and leaves and white highlights along the lit guide lines.
Press Check to see your score and the glaze.
rules: Step one: every fruit must be filled with its own colour (mango yellow, chilli red, tangerine orange, aubergine purple). Score is the share of each fruit that holds the right colour.
Step two: stalks, leaves and highlights are scored by how closely your lines follow the guide in the right colour.
Paint outside a fruit counts against you and the brush lays nothing when it is dry; dip it again.
Guide cycles between lit lines, faint dots and none; Undo takes back the last stroke.
Three stars need a score of 88 or more, two stars 65, one star 40; doing nothing earns no stars.
heritageNote: Luk chup is a sweet of Thailand, shaped by hand into miniature fruit and vegetables. It grew up in the royal kitchens and is now made by home cooks and sold in markets and at celebrations; its bean-paste sweets are related to marzipan fruit brought by traders long ago.
